test_title: RRB NTPC CBT 2 (Level-5) Official Paper (Held On: 15 June 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Embarked upon in 1965-66 as an integral part of the Green Revolution, the High Yielding Varieties Programme (HYVP) included which of the following crops?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Wheat, rice**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The High Yielding Varieties Programme (HYVP),** which was launched in** 1965–1966 as a crucial component** of the so-called** Green Revolution, **was an effort to transform archaic Indian agriculture, particularly with regard to a few crops.
 
• Following the Joint Report on the operation of the HYVP in India, which was published in 1971 by the Programme Evaluation Organisation (PEO) and **the Australian National Academy,** the same team published a more technical and in-depth evaluation of the program's success from 1970 to 1975 in 1976.
 
• The 1976 study, which focused only on wheat and paddy, aimed to clarify the long-term trends in these crops for use in more analytical planning and agricultural research. 
 
• The method used to choose the states, districts, blocks, and villages was the same as the method used in the earlier research.
 
• HYVP area targets of more than one lakh hectares for the Fourth Five Year Plan were granted to the States that grew the chosen crop widely.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The set of research and technology transfer initiatives that took place between 1950 and the late 1960s, known as the **"Green Revolution," or the "Third Agricultural Revolution" (after the Neolithic Revolution and the British Agricultural Revolution)**, increased agricultural production in various parts of the world, starting most noticeably in the late 1960s.
 
• As a result of the activities, new technologies were adopted, including high-yielding (HYV) crop varieties, particularly dwarf wheat and rice.
 
• It was connected to mechanised farming, artificial fertilisers, agrochemicals, controlled water supply (typically using irrigation), and innovative farming techniques.
 
• These were all viewed as a** "bundle of activities" **that could replace** "conventional"** technology and be used as a whole.
